source_text: Nempe cum viventibus loquebatur et his dicebat iustitiam per mysteria fuisse collatam. Quomodo ergo ait eum iustificatum esse, quem mortuum, nisi quia sine aliquo ostendit ambiguo mortem hic abrenuntiationem vocare et ideo a se nomen mortis assumi, ut ostendat ita fideles a peccatis sicut mortuos ab actibus debere cessare?
pass_a_gloss: Namely he was speaking with the living and was saying to these that justice had been conferred through the mysteries. How therefore does he say that he has been justified whom he has said dead, except because without any ambiguity he shows that he here calls death a renunciation and therefore the name of death is taken up by him, so that he may show that the faithful ought so to cease from sins as the dead from acts?

lemmas.lexica: LS iustificatio; Blaise forensic making-just, not later system
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS mors; Blaise temporal vs eternal death in Rom 5

pass_b_english: He was, of course, speaking to living people and telling them that righteousness had been conferred on them through the mysteries. How, then, does he say someone is justified whom he calls dead, unless he is showing beyond ambiguity that here he calls renunciation ‘death’? He adopts the name of death to show that believers should cease from sins as dead people cease from activities.

choices.why: Paul's iustificatio vitae; keep forensic making-just, not a later systematic slogan as default.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
